senses.gloss:
Śyena is the name in the Rigveda of a strong bird of prey, most probably the ‘eagle’; later (as in post-Vedic Sanskrit) it seems to mean the ‘falcon’ or ‘hawk.’ It is the swiftest of birds, and a source of terror to smaller birds. It is the strongest of birds, and even attacks herds. It watches over men (nṛ-cakṣas), a reference, no doubt, to its lofty flight in air. It brings the soma from heaven.
